papers.title: MicroVLA: Edge-Deployable Vision Language Action at 10M Parameters
papers.blurb: 12.4M-parameter VLA: static sentence-embedding lookup for text, Theia-tiny distilled vision encoder, single-shot regression head emitting a 16-step chunk; 90.2% LIBERO, 13.1 ms on a 3090 and 75 ms on CPU. Gap to larger models closed by an ATC-style InfoNCE loss whose gain comes mostly from augmentation.
papers.note: Anonymous workshop preprint; PDF only. Its 'smallest VLA above 90%' claim is superseded by MINERVA.

papers.title: Compact Robot Policies Need Fine-Grained Visual Representations (CoRP)
papers.blurb: 48.9M policy (DINOv2 ViT-S/14, T5-Efficient-Tiny, 48-token FiLM resampler per view, single-block DiT flow head) reaching 97.0% LIBERO and 75.8/73.4 on RoboTwin 2.0. Controlled ablations: pretrained init decisive, freezing costs 19.8 points, a hard token budget beats VIB, language only matters when the scene is ambiguous.
papers.note: Trained on 8 A800 for 8 h (LIBERO). Code promised at camera-ready.

papers.title: MINERVA: How Small Can a Manipulation Policy Be and Still Solve LIBERO?
papers.blurb: 0.54M-parameter policy reaches 95.1% LIBERO; success saturates near 1M parameters and collapses below 0.25M. Vision capacity and chunk length are the only levers that clear the seed-noise band; flow matching shows no gain over one-pass regression. 8.9 ms per chunk on laptop CPU.
papers.note: Closes the parameter-count race on LIBERO.

papers.title: Patch Policy: Efficient Embodied Control via Dense Visual Representations
papers.blurb: Frozen ViT patch tokens fed to a small block-causal transformer policy; dense patches beat pooled or CLS features, reported to surpass fine-tuned OpenVLA-OFT with about 0.7% of its parameters on LIBERO-Goal and three other suites.
papers.note: Contradicts CoRP's frozen-encoder result; evaluated on LIBERO-Goal only.

papers.title: CoRe-WAM: Correspondence-Aligned Temporal Residuals for World Action Models
papers.blurb: Compares current and historical features by correspondence matching and feeds the residual to a lightweight adapter; trains about 1.59M parameters on a frozen Motus visual encoder.

papers.title: Reducing Temporal Redundancy for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference
papers.blurb: Reuses spatial tokens inside the vision encoder across consecutive frames (ViT latency 40.1 to 28.5 ms at 94.4 to 93.9% LIBERO) and pairs it with a 2-step flow policy; most latency savings come from action generation on pi0.5.

papers.title: ActPrune: Action-Grounded Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.blurb: Training-free pruning that derives geometric priors from the previously executed action to drop tokens before the vision encoder runs.

papers.title: Just Noticeable Difference Modeling for Token Compression in Vision-Language-Action Models (Action-JND)
papers.blurb: A token is safe to prune only if removing it keeps the action within a tolerance boundary; prioritizes action-tolerant tokens under a budget.

papers.title: Action ControlNet: A Lightweight Delay-Aware Adapter for Smooth Asynchronous Control in VLA Models
papers.blurb: Treats the already-executed motion suffix as a residual condition for a mostly frozen diffusion or flow action head; few trainable parameters, no backbone change.

papers.title: DEFLECT: Delay-Robust Execution via Flow-matching Likelihood-Estimated Counterfactual Tuning
papers.blurb: Offline post-training that supervises how actions should change as the scene evolves between prediction and execution, filling the gap left by delay-augmented training.

papers.title: Training-Time Action Conditioning for Efficient Real-Time Chunking
papers.blurb: Simulates inference delay during training and conditions on the action prefix directly, removing inference-time inpainting overhead.

papers.title: Understanding Asynchronous Inference Methods for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.blurb: Systematic comparison of asynchronous execution methods (inference-time and training-time RTC, delay augmentation) under controlled delay.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.blurb: Trains with simulated delay by splitting chunks into delay prefix and postfix, plus a separate fast edit policy for reactive correction.

papers.title: TBD-VLA: Temporal Block Diffusion Vision Language Action Model
papers.blurb: Block-diffusion action generation evaluated on LIBERO under injected delay: 97.7% at zero latency, 72.3% at a 4-step delay without real-time chunking, 93.2% with it.

papers.title: LIBERO-Plus: A Progressive Robustness Benchmark for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.blurb: Seven perturbation dimensions (layout, camera, robot initial state, language, lighting, background, sensor noise). Camera and initial-state shifts drop VLAs from 95% to under 30%; models largely ignore language.

papers.title: LIBERO-PRO: Towards Robust and Fair Evaluation of VLA Models Beyond Memorization
papers.blurb: Perturbs objects, initial states, instructions and environments; models above 90% on standard LIBERO fall to 0% in the generalized setting.

papers.title: LoopQ: Fair, Closed-Loop Evaluation of Quantized Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.blurb: Closed-loop evaluation of quantized VLAs with measured per-call latency: quantization saves memory but rarely latency, and losses invisible on LIBERO reappear as 1.5 to 4.3 points under paired LIBERO-Plus perturbations.

papers.title: VLAQuantBench: Closed-Loop Evaluation of Post-Training Quantization for VLA Models
papers.blurb: Benchmark of post-training quantization schemes for VLAs under closed-loop success rather than proxy metrics.

papers.title: When Faster VLA Deployment Changes Closed-Loop Behavior: Task Success-Latency Analysis of SmolVLA Across PyTorch and ONNX Variants
papers.blurb: Argues deployment evaluation must jointly report latency, artifact inspection, interface constraints and closed-loop success; export variants change behavior, not just speed.

papers.title: An Empirical Study on What Matters for Viewpoint-Generalizable Policies in Visual Imitation Learning
papers.blurb: Conditions each visual token on the gripper's 3D position so token-to-gripper geometry is camera-invariant; dense scene features grounded in geometry drive viewpoint generalization.

papers.title: From Fixed to Free Cameras: Calibration-Free View-Robust Vision-Language-Action Model
papers.blurb: View-robust VLA that does not require camera calibration.

papers.title: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action Models are Surprisingly Resistant to Forgetting in Continual Learning
papers.blurb: Continual-learning study on LIBERO with frozen vision and language encoders and trainable action heads in several configurations.

papers.title: CLARE: Continual Learning for VLA Models via Autonomous Adapter Routing and Expansion
papers.blurb: Frozen DINOv2 and CLIP encoders with grown, routed adapters; continual learning of 40 LIBERO tasks without exemplars or task IDs.

papers.title: LifelongVLA: Towards Human-like Physical Intelligence via Lifelong VLA Learning
papers.blurb: Frozen backbone with fast and slow LoRA pathways; reported average forgetting 11.4% versus 19.6% for the strongest baseline.

papers.title: CRL-VLA: Continual Vision-Language-Action Learning
papers.blurb: RL-based continual learning with a shared backbone, decoupled heads, and a frozen critic anchoring old-task values.

papers.title: TinyVLM: Zero-Shot Object Detection on Microcontrollers via Vision-Language Distillation
papers.blurb: Distilled vision encoder of 892 KB after INT8 quantization running on a microcontroller for detection. Adjacent, not a VLA, but the only MCU-class vision-language deployment found.
papers.note: Adjacent work: no manipulation policy has been run closed-loop on an MCU.
